
Question of infections at time zero^[[_NOT FOR PUBLICATION_]{.mark}] {#sec-time-zero}
===================================


Beware when there is an observed removal at time \(0\) _and_ \(I_{0-}{-}R_{0-}{\leq}1\)!

Probably sorted out now, but @sec-monotonicity-CFTP needs checking.

1. In the case of a conditioned activated removal at time \(0\)
(required in applications where the _first_ observed removal
occurs at time zero),
then the prior distribution of the initial \(I_{0-}\) 
should satisfy \(\Prob{I_{0-}{-}R_{0-}>1}{>}0\) if the epidemic is not to die out at time \(0\).

2. If \(R_{0-}{=}0\)
and there is a conditioned removal at time zero,
and if additionally \(I_{0-}{\equiv}1\) (so \(I_{0-}{-}R_0{=}0\)),
then in principle _either_ 
a special infection has to be introduced at time \(0\) which
is activated immediately _or_ the epidemic has to die out immediately.
There would then need to be special provision for proposals to resample the target mark
of the initial infection, in order to ensure irreducibility for the \CFTP.
Thus a Bayesian prior (for \(I_{0-}\))
that does not respect the observed behaviour of the epidemic
can be fixed by introducing an infection at time \(0\),
but only at the cost of complicating the algorithm to require
re-sampling of the target mark of such an infection!

3. I argue that a principled Bayesian argument is preferable:
if the epidemic may not die out immediately then 
the prior distribution of \(I_{0-}\) ought to give positive chance
to \(I_{0-}{>}1\). Updates carried out using the algorithm would
then _never_ choose \(I_{0-}{=}1\), as free innovations would 
never supply an infection at \(0\) and therefore a choice of \(I_{0-}{=}1\)
would lead to conditioned removals not being observed!
